grades.question: What makes a normal move legal, can the same warriors move repeatedly, and do rivers count as paths?
grades.expected_answer: Move more than zero warriors/pawns along one linking path to an adjacent clearing; rule origin or destination or both. Same pieces can move repeatedly. Rivers are not paths unless explicitly treated as such.

observed.answer: A normal move takes any positive number of the mover’s warriors or pawns along a linking path from one clearing to an adjacent clearing, and the mover must rule the origin, destination, or both. Rule is rechecked for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including in multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.

grades.question: Describe battle from ambush through removal: foiling, early ending, dice limits, extra hits, removal priorities and who scores removed buildings/tokens.
grades.expected_answer: Defender may ambush matching clearing; attacker may foil with matching ambush. Unfoiled ambush deals two immediate hits; discard defender ambush, end battle if no attacking warriors/pawns remain. Before-roll effects, roll high attacker/low defender, rolled hits capped by own warriors, after-roll effects, count hits including uncapped extra hits and defenseless extra attacker hit if no defending warriors, then deal hits. Each side chooses own removals, warriors first. Whoever removes enemy building/token scores one, including defender.

observed.answer: The defender may play one matching-suit Ambush (birds are wild). The attacker may foil it with a matching Ambush; the defender’s card is discarded and a foiled Ambush deals no hits. Otherwise the defender immediately deals two hits and discards the card. If no attacking warriors or Vagabond pawn remain, battle ends immediately. Resolve before-roll effects, roll, after-roll effects, count hits, then deal hits. Higher die is the attacker’s rolled hits and lower die the defender’s (equal dice give equal results); each side’s rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle. Alliance defense reverses the dice; the Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors. Add extra hits without a warrior cap and subtract ignored hits; an attacker gets one defenseless hit if the defender has no warriors, or if the defender is the Vagabond and has no undamaged swords. Each hit removes an opposing piece. The side taking hits chooses its removal order, but must remove all its warriors before buildings or tokens. Both sides deal their counted hits even if warriors are removed during that step. Whoever removes an enemy building or token scores one VP each, even when defending or outside battle. Vagabond hits damage items.
observed.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle, ‘Battle (4.3)’ steps 1–6.

grades.question: How does the Eyrie resolve its Decree, including action suit locations, within-column order and Build restrictions?
grades.expected_answer: Craft first; resolve all cards Recruit,Move,Battle,Build in that column order, cards in any order within column. Recruit at matching roost; Move from matching clearing with at least one warrior; Battle in matching clearing; Build in matching ruled clearing without roost and open slot. Bird wild. Inability fully resolve immediately causes turmoil.

observed.answer: The Eyrie crafts with roosts first, then resolves every Decree card column by column in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order. Within each column it chooses the card order freely; birds are wild. Recruit places a warrior (two with Charismatic) at a roost in a clearing matching the card's suit. Move requires moving at least one warrior from a matching clearing, subject to ordinary movement rules. Battle requires initiating a battle in a matching clearing with Eyrie warriors and an enemy. Build requires placing a roost in a matching clearing the Eyrie rules, with an open slot and no roost already there. If any required action cannot be fully completed, the Eyrie immediately enters Turmoil and cannot skip that card or continue other columns.
observed.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Daylight — resolve the Decree.

grades.question: When does Outrage trigger, what is paid, and what if the player has no matching card or the supporter stack is full?
grades.expected_answer: Another player removing sympathy or moving any warriors into sympathetic clearing owes one matching hand card including bird to supporters. Merely battling without removing sympathy is not trigger. If none matching show hand to Alliance; Alliance draws deck card to supporters. No bases caps stack at five; incoming overflow discarded.

observed.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one hand card matching the clearing to Supporters, with birds counting; a group move costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. If the player has no matching card, including birds, they show their hand to the Alliance, which draws one card from the deck into Supporters. Supporter capacity still applies: with no base, the stack is capped at five and incoming cards beyond capacity are discarded; with any base, it is unlimited. Merely battling in a sympathetic clearing does not trigger Outrage unless sympathy is removed, and moving only the Vagabond pawn does not trigger it.
observed.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Supporters and Outrage.

grades.question: How do Alliance Revolt and Spread Sympathy differ in timing/order, eligible clearing, supporter cost, martial law and results?

Spread: unsympathetic adjacent to sympathy or any clearing if none; pay shown matching supporters plus one if at least three warriors of one other player; place sympathy and score uncovered points.

observed.answer: In Birdsong, the Alliance may Revolt any number of times first, then Spread Sympathy any number of times. Revolt chooses a sympathetic clearing without a base matching a base still on the Alliance board, spends two matching supporters, removes all enemy pieces there, places the matching base, places warriors equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching that base's printed suit, and places one warrior in the Officers box. Spread Sympathy chooses an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if no sympathy is on the map; it spends the matching supporters shown above the next sympathy token, plus one matching supporter for Martial Law if one other player has at least three warriors there, then places sympathy and scores the uncovered VP. Revolt and Spread Sympathy are different actions with these separate eligibility and cost rules.

grades.question: How do Vagabond refresh, Slip, normal Move and forest Rest work, including hostile destinations and Evening drawing?
grades.expected_answer: Refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on track, then three more; newly refreshed tea does not boost that step. Forest Rest repairs all damaged items and flips them face up; still draw one plus face-up coins on track then discard to five.

observed.answer: At Birdsong, refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed during this step gives no bonus refresh in that step. The Vagabond may then Slip to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, including into hostile warriors, ignoring effects that prevent movement out of a clearing. A normal Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra boot if the destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. If the Vagabond is in a forest in Evening, Rest returns damaged items to the Satchel and flips them face up, with ready tea/coins/bags moving to tracks if possible; Rest does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. It always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on track, even after Rest.

grades.question: When does a faction become Hostile to Vagabond, when is Infamy scored, can Aid undo Hostility, and what does Strike target?
grades.expected_answer: Removing any one non-hostile faction warrior makes Hostile. Infamy one extra VP per hostile piece removed in battle during own turn except warrior causing hostility; no Infamy for Strike. Aid cannot undo hostility but can take crafted item. Strike exhaust crossbow, removes enemy warrior, or other faction piece if that enemy has no warriors there.

observed.answer: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes that faction Hostile to the Vagabond. During battle on the Vagabond's own turn, Infamy scores one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made the faction Hostile; ordinary points for buildings/tokens still apply. Infamy is not scored while defending on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a faction out of Hostile, though it can still obtain a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing; only if that enemy has no warriors there may it remove another piece of that faction. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.

grades.question: What are coalition eligibility, timing, VP requirement, partner selection and victory, and what changes if partner is Hostile?
grades.expected_answer: Vagabond cannot use normal dominance win. With four or more players during own Daylight at least 10 VP activates dominance to coalition with lowest VP other player not already in coalition, choose tied lowest. Place score marker on partner board, stop scoring; partner win means Vagabond also wins. Hostile partner relationship becomes Indifferent.

observed.answer: The Vagabond cannot activate normal dominance to win. With four or more players, during its own Daylight at 10 or more VP, it may activate a dominance card to form a coalition with a player not already in a coalition who has the lowest VP among players other than the Vagabond; it chooses among ties. It places its score marker on that player's faction board and stops scoring. If the partner wins, the Vagabond also wins, including when the partner wins by dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies, and a Hostile partner becomes Indifferent; coalition alone does not grant Allied relationship powers.
